problem: The reason given for treating distillation as equimolar counter-diffusion is imprecise. That assumption rests on the two components having nearly equal molar latent heats of vaporisation (equimolar overflow), not on their boiling points being close. A student may write 'close boiling points' as the justification in an exam.
fix: Distillation of a binary mixture whose components have nearly equal molar latent heats (equimolar overflow, as with benzene and toluene) is often treated this way.

problem: The stated reason for needing Maxwell-Stefan is wrong for a binary mixture. A concentrated binary mixture still needs only one pair diffusivity; the Maxwell-Stefan set becomes necessary when there are three or more components, and when strong thermodynamic non-ideality must be included.
fix: Mixtures of three or more components need the Maxwell-Stefan equations, because one diffusivity per pair is not enough to describe them; strongly non-ideal mixtures also need activity-coefficient corrections.
